#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/adversarial-review-budget.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 3 Task 3.3 (PRD FR-7 AC-7.5, SDD D-7.4, D-7.6).
#
# The dissent budget pre-check prices every planned voice — the primary, the companion's first hop, each advisory voice —
# at its catalog price (python3 -m loa_cheval.metering.pricing --alias), instead of the fixed 10 / 30 USD per Mtok.
# An alias with no catalog price falls back to 10 / 30 for that voice and is said by name; a zero-priced entry estimates
# zero and is said too. Prices come from fixture entries in the test's project config (hounfour.providers overlays the
# catalog, as cheval merges it). Each voice: input tokens × input rate + 2000 × output rate, micro-USD/Mtok → cents.
# =============================================================================

load adversarial-review-s3-helpers

setup() { export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"; s3_setup sprint-s3bud; }   # (the CLI lock is this test's own — CMP-121)
teardown() { s3_teardown; }

_cfg() {  # <model> <budget> <companion_voice> [extra code_review lines]
    s3_config "hounfour:
  providers:
    openai:
      models:
        fixture-priced:
          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 2000000, output_per_mtok: 8000000}
    fixturelocal:
      models:
        fixture-zero:
          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 0, output_per_mtok: 0}
        fixture-stale:
          price_date: \"2000-01-01\"
          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 1000000, output_per_mtok: 1000000}
flatline_protocol:
  code_review:
    enabled: true
    model: $1
    budget_cents: $2
    timeout_seconds: 30
    companion_voice: $3
    fallback_chain: []
${4:-}"
}

_big_diff() {  # a diff whose estimate is 1,000,500 input tokens (3,000,000 bytes / 3 + 500)
    { printf 'diff --git a/x.sh b/x.sh\n'; head -c $(( 3000000 - 25 )) /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'a'; } > "$T/diff.patch"
    [ "$(wc -c < "$T/diff.patch")" -eq 3000000 ]
}

@test "BUD-1 the primary is priced at its catalog rate (no fixed-rate fallback): 1,000,500 tokens × 2 + 2000 × 8 USD/Mtok = 201c" {
    _big_diff
    _cfg fixture-priced 150 false
    result=$(s3_run review)
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.status' <<<"$result")" = "budget_exceeded" ]
    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "201" ]
    [ "$(jq -c '[.metadata.estimate_voices[] | {role, alias, estimated_cents, pricing_source}]' <<<"$result")" = '[{"role":"primary","alias":"fixture-priced","estimated_cents":201,"pricing_source":"config"}]' ]
    grep -qF "budget: estimate 201c over 1 planned voice(s) (primary fixture-priced 201c)" "$T/stderr.log"
    ! grep -q "no catalog price" "$T/stderr.log" || { echo "a catalog-priced primary fell back"; return 1; }
    [ ! -s "$CALLS" ]
}

@test "BUD-2 an alias with no catalog price falls back to 10 / 30 USD per Mtok for that voice, said by name (1000c + 6c)" {
    _big_diff
    _cfg mystery-model-x 150 false
    result=$(s3_run review)
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ]
    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "1006" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.estimate_voices[0].pricing_source' <<<"$result")" = "fallback" ]
    grep -qF "budget: no catalog price for mystery-model-x (primary) — the fixed 10 / 30 USD per Mtok applies to this voice" "$T/stderr.log"
    [ "$(grep -c "no catalog price" "$T/stderr.log")" = "1" ]
}

@test "BUD-3 a zero-priced entry estimates 0c and is said: a 0-cent budget admits it, where the fixed rate would refuse" {
    _cfg fixture-zero 0 false
    s3_run review >/dev/null
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    grep -qF "budget: fixture-zero (primary) is zero-priced in the catalog — estimated 0c" "$T/stderr.log"
    grep -qF "budget: estimate 0c over 1 planned voice(s) (primary fixture-zero 0c)" "$T/stderr.log"
    grep -qx "fixture-zero" "$CALLS"
    # the same run priced at the fixed rate is refused (the regression this replaces: 2000 output tokens × 30 = 6c > 0)
    _cfg mystery-model-x 0 false
    s3_run review >/dev/null
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ]
}

@test "BUD-4 the gate sums every planned voice: primary + the companion's first hop + each advisory voice" {
    _big_diff
    _cfg fixture-priced 1 true "    advisory_voices: [fixture-zero, mystery-model-x]"
    result=$(s3_run review)
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    [ "$(jq -r '[.metadata.estimate_voices[] | "\(.role)=\(.alias)"] | join(" ")' <<<"$result")" = "primary=fixture-priced companion=claude-headless advisory=fixture-zero advisory=mystery-model-x" ]
    # the companion's price is the catalog's (whatever it is today): recompute it from the same CLI
    local row ci co comp
    row=$(PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 PYTHONPATH="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/adapters" python3 -W ignore::RuntimeWarning -m loa_cheval.metering.pricing --alias claude-headless --config "$CONFIG_FILE")
    ci=$(sed -n 's/.* input_per_mtok=\([0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$row"); co=$(sed -n 's/.* output_per_mtok=\([0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$row")
    [[ "$ci" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$co" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]
    comp=$(( 1000500 * ci / 10000000000 + 2000 * co / 10000000000 ))
    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimate_voices[1].estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "$comp" ]
    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimate_voices[2].estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "0" ]
    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimate_voices[3].estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "1006" ]
    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "$(( 201 + comp + 0 + 1006 ))" ]
    [ "$(jq '[.metadata.estimate_voices[].estimated_cents] | add' <<<"$result")" = "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" ]
    grep -qF "budget: fixture-zero (advisory) is zero-priced in the catalog — estimated 0c" "$T/stderr.log"
    grep -qF "budget: no catalog price for mystery-model-x (advisory)" "$T/stderr.log"
}

@test "BUD-5 a stale catalog price (price_date older than 90 days) is used as given and said" {
    _cfg fixture-stale 1000 false
    s3_run review >/dev/null
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    grep -qF "budget: fixture-stale (primary) has a stale catalog price (price_date older than 90 days) — used as given" "$T/stderr.log"
}

@test "BUD-6 with no price CLI answer at all every voice falls back and is said (the gate never prices from nothing)" {
    _cfg fixture-priced 1000 false
    # a PYTHONPATH that cannot import the package: the CLI fails, every planned voice is unknown
    local real patched
    real="$(declare -f _adv_budget_estimate)"
    patched="${real/PYTHONPATH=\"\$PROJECT_ROOT\/.claude\/adapters\"/PYTHONPATH=/nonexistent}"
    [ "$patched" != "$real" ]   # (the seam was found: the CLI really cannot be imported in this run)
    eval "$patched"
    s3_run review >/dev/null
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ]
    grep -qF "budget: no catalog price for fixture-priced (primary)" "$T/stderr.log"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/adversarial-review-locality.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 3 Task 3.5 (PRD FR-8 AC-8.1 … AC-8.3, SDD D-8.0 … D-8.2,
# DEC-0146).
#
# Under hounfour.locality: local_voices, adversarial-review.sh plans only hops whose provider has dispatch_group: local in
# the merged config (catalog + the project's hounfour.providers) and refuses every hosted hop of its inventory at plan time
# by name — primary chain, companion chain, advisory voices, the KF-004 repair chain (tiny, claude-headless, any pin; the
# chain is the answering voice). With one local family the audit is DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW, the gate and verdict-derive
# treat the envelope as today, and the output says so. The default (hosted) is unchanged. Mock mode: the harness stub.
# =============================================================================

load adversarial-review-s3-helpers

setup() { export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"; s3_setup sprint-s3loc; }   # (the CLI lock is this test's own — CMP-121)
teardown() { s3_teardown; }

# one hosted provider (openai, the catalog's) and one local provider (localbox, declared here)
_cfg() {  # <locality value | absent> [extra code_review / security_audit lines]
    local loc=""; [[ "$1" == absent ]] || loc="  locality: $1"
    s3_config "hounfour:
$loc
  providers:
    localbox:
      type: openai_compat
      endpoint: \"http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1\"
      models:
        qwen-local:
          dispatch_group: local
          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 0, output_per_mtok: 0}
        qwen-local-b:
          dispatch_group: local
          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 0, output_per_mtok: 0}
        qwen-local-c:
          dispatch_group: local
        qwen-leaky:
          dispatch_group: local
          fallback_chain: [\"openai:gpt-5.5\"]
  aliases:
    lq: \"localbox:qwen-local\"
    lqb: \"localbox:qwen-local-b\"
    lqc: \"localbox:qwen-local-c\"
flatline_protocol:
  code_review:
    enabled: true
    model: gpt-5.5
    budget_cents: 500
    timeout_seconds: 30
    fallback_chain: [lq]
${2:-}
  security_audit:
    enabled: true
    model: gpt-5.5
    budget_cents: 500
    timeout_seconds: 30
    fallback_chain: [lq]
${3:-}"
}

_hosted_in() {  # <file of hop names, one per line> → the hosted ones, as hop-locality.py classifies them against this config
    local hops; hops=$(sed 's/^repair://' "$1" | sort -u | grep -v '^$' || true)
    [[ -n "$hops" ]] || return 0
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    python3 -I "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py" --catalog "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml" \
        --config "$CONFIG_FILE" -- $hops | awk -F'\t' '$3 != "local" { print $1 }'
}

@test "LOC-1 one hosted and one local provider: only the local hop is planned and every hosted hop is refused by name" {
    _cfg local_voices
    result=$(s3_run review)
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    env="$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json"
    # the dispatched hops: the local one only
    [ "$(sort -u "$CALLS" | tr '\n' ' ')" = "lq " ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.final_model' "$env")" = "lq" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.model_attempts | join(",")' "$env")" = "lq:reviewed" ]
    # each refusal named: the hosted primary, the companion's default hop, the repair chain's two hosted hops
    grep -qxF "[adversarial-review] locality: local_voices refuses hosted hop gpt-5.5 (openai)" "$T/stderr.log"
    grep -qxF "[adversarial-review] locality: local_voices refuses hosted hop claude-headless (anthropic)" "$T/stderr.log"
    grep -qxF "[adversarial-review] locality: local_voices refuses hosted hop tiny (anthropic)" "$T/stderr.log"
    # the companion was not planned: its chain had no local hop — never rerouted
    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.companion_voice.planned' "$env")" = "false" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.companion_voice.reason' "$env")" = "locality_refused" ]
    # the envelope names the posture and each refusal with its role
    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.locality.mode' "$env")" = "local_voices" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '[.metadata.locality.refused[] | "\(.role):\(.alias):\(.provider)"] | sort | join(" ")' "$env")" = \
      "companion:claude-headless:anthropic primary:gpt-5.5:openai repair:claude-headless:anthropic repair:tiny:anthropic" ]
    [ "$(jq '.verdict_quality.voices_planned' "$env")" = "1" ]
}

@test "LOC-2 the repair chain is pinned to the answering local voice: no tiny, no claude-headless, no pin — even with an Anthropic key" {
    _cfg local_voices
    export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="fixture-not-a-key"   # (tiny would lead the hosted chain with a key present)
    export LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL="tiny claude-headless"
    load_adversarial_config review
    [ "$CONF_LOCALITY" = "local_voices" ]
    [ "$(_repair_model_chain lq)" = "lq" ]
    [ "$(_repair_chain_base lq)" = "lq" ]
    [ "$(_repair_model_chain gpt-5.5)" = "" ]   # (a hosted answering voice gets no repair hop at all)
    # and under hosted the same host walks tiny first (the switch is what pins it)
    _cfg hosted
    load_adversarial_config review
    [ "$(_repair_model_chain lq)" = "tiny claude-headless" ]   # (the operator pin is the whole chain under hosted)
    unset LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL
    [ "$(_repair_model_chain lq)" = "tiny claude-headless lq" ]
}

@test "LOC-3 redaction-style: in a whole run with a rejected payload, an Anthropic key and the CLIs present, no hosted alias is ever dispatched" {
    _cfg local_voices "    advisory_voices: [lqc, gpt-5.5-pro]
    companion_chain:
      anthropic: [opus, lqb]"
    export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="fixture-not-a-key" OPENAI_API_KEY="fixture-not-a-key"
    _repair_finding_via_model() { echo "repair:$4" >> "$CALLS"; return 1; }
    BEHAVIOUR[lq]=reject
    s3_run review >/dev/null
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    env="$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json"
    [ -s "$CALLS" ]
    grep -qx "repair:lq" "$CALLS"   # (the repair loop ran — pinned to the answering voice)
    [ "$(_hosted_in "$CALLS")" = "" ] || { echo "hosted hops dispatched:"; _hosted_in "$CALLS"; return 1; }
    # no hosted name in any planned hop the envelope records
    local planned
    planned=$(jq -r '[.metadata.model_attempts[], (.metadata.companion_voice.chain // [])[], (.advisory_voices // [] | map(select(.status != "refused")) | .[].alias)] | .[] | sub(":[a-z_]+$"; "")' "$env")
    printf '%s\n' "$planned" > "$T/planned"
    [ "$(_hosted_in "$T/planned")" = "" ] || { echo "hosted hops planned:"; _hosted_in "$T/planned"; return 1; }
    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.companion_voice.chain | join(",")' "$env")" = "lqb" ]
    grep -qxF "[adversarial-review] locality: local_voices refuses hosted hop opus (anthropic)" "$T/stderr.log"
    grep -qxF "[adversarial-review] locality: local_voices refuses hosted hop gpt-5.5-pro (openai)" "$T/stderr.log"
    # the refused advisory voice is named in the block, never run
    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[] | select(.alias == "gpt-5.5-pro") | .status' "$env")" = "refused" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[] | select(.alias == "lqc") | .status' "$env")" = "succeeded" ]
    ! grep -qx "gpt-5.5-pro" "$CALLS" || { echo "a refused advisory voice was dispatched"; return 1; }
}

@test "LOC-4 one local family on the audit gate: the companion is duplicate_voice, the DEGRADED sentence is in the output, and the gate and verdict-derive treat the envelope as today" {
    _cfg local_voices "" "    companion_chain:
      anthropic: [lqb]"
    s3_run audit >/dev/null
    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
    env="$OUT_DIR/adversarial-audit.json"
    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.companion_voice.counted_as' "$env")" = "duplicate_voice" ]
    local s="locality: local_voices — with one local family the companion is not an independent second voice (duplicate_voice, or not planned), so every security audit is DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW; adversarial-review-gate.sh and verdict-derive.sh treat this envelope exactly as they treat any other."
    grep -qxF "[adversarial-review] $s" "$T/stderr.log"
    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.locality.note' "$env")" = "$s" ]
    # the config comment carries the same sentence
    grep -qF "$s" "$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml.example"

    local hook="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh" cfg="$T/gate.yaml" rc=0

    [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]

    printf '%s\n' "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" '' 'DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW: one local family (locality: local_voices).' \

class _Stub:
    """127.0.0.1 HTTP server the test starts and stops. Paths: /v1/ok (200 JSON),
    /v1/redirect (302 to /v1/ok), /v1/stream (one SSE chunk). Records request headers."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        stub = self
        self.seen: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []

        class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def _reply(self) -> None:
                length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
                if length:
                    self.rfile.read(length)
                stub.seen.append({"path": self.path, "headers": dict(self.headers)})
                if self.path.endswith("/redirect"):
                    self.send_response(302)
                    self.send_header("Location", f"http://127.0.0.1:{stub.port}/v1/ok")
                    self.send_header("Content-Length", "0")
                    self.end_headers()
                    return
                payload = b'{"ok": true}'
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
                self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(payload)))
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(payload)

            do_GET = _reply
            do_POST = _reply

            def log_message(self, *args: Any) -> None:
                pass

        self.server = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
        self.port = self.server.server_port
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)

    def __enter__(self) -> "_Stub":
        self.thread.start()
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc: Any) -> None:
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()

    @property
    def endpoint(self) -> str:
        return f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.port}/v1"

def _policy(s: _Stub) -> TransportPolicy:

def test_redirect_refused(transport, stub):
    with pytest.raises(InvalidConfigError, match="redirect refused"):
        http_post(f"{stub.endpoint}/redirect", {}, {"x": 1}, policy=_policy(stub))
    with pytest.raises(InvalidConfigError, match="redirect refused"):

    with pytest.raises(InvalidConfigError, match="redirect refused"):

_PROXY_VARS = ("HTTP_PROXY", "HTTPS_PROXY", "ALL_PROXY", "http_proxy", "https_proxy", "all_proxy")


def test_proxy_env_ignored(transport, stub, monkeypatch):
    import urllib.request

    for var in ("NO_PROXY", "no_proxy"):
        monkeypatch.delenv(var, raising=False)
    for var in _PROXY_VARS:
        monkeypatch.setenv(var, "http://127.0.0.1:1")   # a dead proxy: any use of it fails
    # urllib caches a process-wide default opener whose ProxyHandler read the env when it
    # was built; drop it so the no-policy control below sees this test's proxy env.
    monkeypatch.setattr(urllib.request, "_opener", None)
    status, body = http_post(f"{stub.endpoint}/ok", {}, {"x": 1}, policy=_policy(stub))
    assert (status, body) == (200, {"ok": True})
    status, _ = http_get(f"{stub.endpoint}/ok", {}, policy=_policy(stub))
    assert status == 200
    with http_post_stream(f"{stub.endpoint}/ok", {}, {"x": 1}, policy=_policy(stub)) as resp:
        assert resp.status_code == 200 and b"".join(resp.iter_bytes()) == b'{"ok": true}'
    # control: without the policy the same call goes to the dead proxy and never reaches the stub
    seen_before = len(stub.seen)
    try:
        control_status: Optional[int] = http_post(f"{stub.endpoint}/ok", {}, {"x": 1})[0]
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — httpx raises ConnectionLostError; urllib returns 503
        control_status = None
    assert control_status != 200
    assert len(stub.seen) == seen_before

"""cycle-129 FR-7 (SDD D-7.2; sprint-257 Task 3.1, AC-3.1) — the per-provider
insecure-endpoint opt-in on BOTH paths, and the request-time rules.

* One case table runs through the bash-path validator
  (`.claude/scripts/lib/endpoint-validator.py` `validate(..., allow_insecure_endpoint=...)`)
  and the cheval Python path (`loa_cheval.config.endpoint_policy.check_endpoint`); the two
  must agree on accept/refuse and on the refusal code.
* D-7.2 test list: IPv4 and IPv6 loopback accepted, RFC1918 accepted, link-local and metadata
  refused, DNS name refused, boolean refused, cross-provider isolation, and — at request time
  against a stub server bound to 127.0.0.1 — redirect refused, proxy env ignored, path prefix
  enforced, on the httpx and the urllib transport.

def test_cross_provider_isolation_on_both_paths():
    """Provider A's opt-in is passed with A's URL only; provider B (same loopback host, no
    opt-in of its own) keeps every refusal on both paths, before and after A is validated."""
    a_url, a_optin = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1", "127.0.0.1"
    b_url = "http://127.0.0.1:9000/v1"
    for _ in range(2):
        assert _cheval(a_url, a_optin) is OK and _bash_path(a_url, a_optin) is OK
        assert _cheval(b_url, None) == "ENDPOINT-INSECURE-SCHEME"
        assert _bash_path(b_url, None) == "ENDPOINT-INSECURE-SCHEME"
    # the hosted provider's https URL is untouched by A's opt-in
    assert _bash_path("https://api.openai.com/v1", None) is OK
    assert _bash_path("https://api.openai.com/v1", a_optin) is OK


# --- request time: a stub server on 127.0.0.1 -------------------------------------------------------------


class _Stub:
    """127.0.0.1 HTTP server the test starts and stops. Paths: /v1/ok (200 JSON),
    /v1/redirect (302 to /v1/ok), /v1/stream (one SSE chunk). Records request headers."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        stub = self
        self.seen: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []

        class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def _reply(self) -> None:
                length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
                if length:
                    self.rfile.read(length)
                stub.seen.append({"path": self.path, "headers": dict(self.headers)})
                if self.path.endswith("/redirect"):
                    self.send_response(302)
                    self.send_header("Location", f"http://127.0.0.1:{stub.port}/v1/ok")
                    self.send_header("Content-Length", "0")
                    self.end_headers()
                    return
                payload = b'{"ok": true}'
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
                self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(payload)))
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(payload)

            do_GET = _reply
            do_POST = _reply

            def log_message(self, *args: Any) -> None:
                pass

        self.server = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
        self.port = self.server.server_port
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)

    def __enter__(self) -> "_Stub":
        self.thread.start()
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc: Any) -> None:
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()

    @property
    def endpoint(self) -> str:
        return f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.port}/v1"

        http_post(f"{stub.endpoint}/redirect", {}, {"x": 1}, policy=_policy(stub))
    with pytest.raises(InvalidConfigError, match="redirect refused"):
        http_get(f"{stub.endpoint}/redirect", {}, policy=_policy(stub))
    with pytest.raises(InvalidConfigError, match="redirect refused"):
        with http_post_stream(f"{stub.endpoint}/redirect", {}, {"x": 1}, policy=_policy(stub)):
            pass
    # never followed: the stub saw only the redirecting request, never /v1/ok
    assert all(r["path"].endswith("/redirect") for r in stub.seen)


_PROXY_VARS = ("HTTP_PROXY", "HTTPS_PROXY", "ALL_PROXY", "http_proxy", "https_proxy", "all_proxy")


def test_proxy_env_ignored(transport, stub, monkeypatch):
    import urllib.request

    for var in ("NO_PROXY", "no_proxy"):
        monkeypatch.delenv(var, raising=False)
    for var in _PROXY_VARS:
        monkeypatch.setenv(var, "http://127.0.0.1:1")   # a dead proxy: any use of it fails
    # urllib caches a process-wide default opener whose ProxyHandler read the env when it
    # was built; drop it so the no-policy control below sees this test's proxy env.
    monkeypatch.setattr(urllib.request, "_opener", None)
    status, body = http_post(f"{stub.endpoint}/ok", {}, {"x": 1}, policy=_policy(stub))
    assert (status, body) == (200, {"ok": True})
    status, _ = http_get(f"{stub.endpoint}/ok", {}, policy=_policy(stub))
    assert status == 200
    with http_post_stream(f"{stub.endpoint}/ok", {}, {"x": 1}, policy=_policy(stub)) as resp:
        assert resp.status_code == 200 and b"".join(resp.iter_bytes()) == b'{"ok": true}'
    # control: without the policy the same call goes to the dead proxy and never reaches the stub
    seen_before = len(stub.seen)
    try:
        control_status: Optional[int] = http_post(f"{stub.endpoint}/ok", {}, {"x": 1})[0]
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — httpx raises ConnectionLostError; urllib returns 503
        control_status = None
    assert control_status != 200
    assert len(stub.seen) == seen_before


@pytest.mark.parametrize("url", [
    "/other/chat/completions",          # outside the declared path
    "/v10/chat/completions",            # a sibling that only shares the prefix string
    "/v1/../admin",                     # traversal
])
def test_path_prefix_enforced(stub, url):
    with pytest.raises(InvalidConfigError, match="outside the declared endpoint"):
        http_post(f"http://127.0.0.1:{stub.port}{url}", {}, {}, policy=_policy(stub))
    assert stub.seen == []


def test_origin_must_match(stub):
    pol = _policy(stub)
    for url in (f"http://127.0.0.1:{stub.port + 1}/v1/x", f"http://localhost:{stub.port}/v1/x",
                f"https://127.0.0.1:{stub.port}/v1/x"):
        with pytest.raises(InvalidConfigError):
            pol.check_url(url)
    pol.check_url(f"{stub.endpoint}/chat/completions")
    pol.check_url(stub.endpoint)


def test_opted_in_adapter_sends_no_credential_and_uses_the_policy(stub, monkeypatch):
    """A keyless opted-in provider: the OpenAI adapter's request carries no Authorization
    header and goes through the TransportPolicy (dead proxy env set; still reaches the stub)."""
    from loa_cheval.providers.openai_adapter import OpenAIAdapter
    from loa_cheval.types import CompletionRequest, ModelConfig, ProviderConfig

    for var in _PROXY_VARS:
        monkeypatch.setenv(var, "http://127.0.0.1:1")
    monkeypatch.setenv("LOA_CHEVAL_DISABLE_STREAMING", "1")
    cfg = ProviderConfig(
        name="local", type="openai_compat", endpoint=stub.endpoint, auth="",
        keyless=True, allow_insecure_endpoint="127.0.0.1",
        models={"m": ModelConfig(capabilities=["chat"], context_window=32768, endpoint_family="chat",
                                 dispatch_group="local")},
    )
    adapter = OpenAIAdapter(cfg)
    assert adapter.validate_config() == []
    # the stub answers {"ok": true}: no `choices`, so the parse fails AFTER the request
    with pytest.raises(Exception, match="no choices"):
        adapter.complete(CompletionRequest(messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}], model="m", max_tokens=16))
    assert len(stub.seen) == 1
    assert stub.seen[0]["path"] == "/v1/chat/completions"
    assert "Authorization" not in stub.seen[0]["headers"]

head/.claude/loa/reference/scripts-reference.md:73 — Documents that `model-health-probe.sh` "refuses a hosted probe under `local_voices`", but the script has no locality handling at all (it never reads `hounfour.locality`); under `local_voices` the probe still sends requests to hosted providers. Either implement the plan-time refusal in the probe or drop the claim from this row, from `.loa.config.yaml.example` and from the multi-model reference.
head/.loa.config.yaml.example:818 — The `hounfour.locality` comment promises that "the health probe is planned only on a provider whose model entry says `dispatch_group: local`"; `model-health-probe.sh` does not implement this (see the scripts-reference finding), so the operator-facing config comment overstates the posture.
head/.claude/loa/reference/multi-model-reference.md:102 — States that "health-probe hops are planned only on providers whose model entry says `dispatch_group: local`" under `local_voices`; the probe has no such gate, so this reference describes behaviour the PR does not ship.
head/.claude/loa/reference/scripts-reference.md:74 — The `lib/hop-locality.py` row gives exit codes "0 local; 1 hosted or unresolved; 2 usage", but `main()` always returns 0 and reports the classification only on stdout (verified: a run with hosted and unresolved hops exits 0). Callers reading this table would misinterpret the exit status; document "0 (classification on stdout); 2 usage" or implement the codes.
head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:482 — `parseProviderDecls` treats any literal `auth` value (anything without `{env:`) as keyless, while the D-8.0 rule the cheval loader implements (`KEYLESS_AUTH_LITERALS = {"local"}` in `loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py:50`) normalises only the literal `"local"` because any other literal could be a real key. A trusted provider with a literal key is therefore reported as a "keyless provider" in the startup line and admitted without any credential check, and the two implementations of the same rule disagree.
head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/audit/modelinv.py:473 — `hop_locality_of` reads only the model entry's `dispatch_group`, whereas `lib/hop-locality.py` (`classify`) and Bridgebuilder's `isLocalVoice` also honour a provider-level `dispatch_group: local` (the trusted-config test relies on it). A hop the shell planners treat as local is recorded as `hop_locality: hosted` in MODELINV; `OpenAIAdapter._transport_policy` has the same model-only check, so such a hop also misses the D-7.2 request-time rules unless `allow_insecure_endpoint` is set. The three readers of D-8.0 should share one definition.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED
EOF

content.text:
Review written to `review.md`. Verdict: **CHANGES_REQUIRED**.

**What I did.** I read the full diff (80 files: the dissent script, cheval adapters, Bridgebuilder TypeScript and its dist build, Flatline, the health probe, the endpoint validator, config, schemas, docs, and all new bats and pytest suites). I verified that every helper the new shell code calls exists with the expected signature, ran the new hop-locality classifier and the pricing CLI against the head catalog, ran the head endpoint validator over every declared catalog endpoint, and confirmed the dist build mirrors the TypeScript sources. The large pieces (advisory voices, catalog-priced budget gate, locality planning in the dissent and Flatline, the TransportPolicy, keyless providers, thinking-strip, the trusted-config reader, exit code 3 and its callers) are internally consistent and match their tests.

**Findings (7 lines in review.md).**

- **Probe cannot reach hosted configured providers.** `_probe_configured` runs the URL through the fixed provider allowlist, so only an opted-in loopback or RFC1918 host passes. The documented Azure-style configured provider is refused as `ENDPOINT-HOST-NOT-ALLOWED`. The loader admits the same endpoint via the declared-endpoint rule.
- **Documented locality gate in the probe does not exist.** The scripts reference, the example config comment, and the multi-model reference all say the health probe refuses hosted hops under `local_voices`. The script never reads `hounfour.locality`. This overstates the security posture the PR ships.
- **Wrong exit codes documented** for `hop-locality.py`. It always exits 0 and classifies on stdout.
- **Two implementations of the keyless rule disagree.** Bridgebuilder treats any literal `auth` as keyless. The cheval loader normalises only the literal `local`, for the stated reason that any other literal could be a real key.
- **Three readers of `dispatch_group: local` disagree.** The shell classifier and Bridgebuilder honour a provider-level group. The MODELINV telemetry and the adapter's transport-policy check read only the model entry.

**What's next.** The two probe items are the blocking ones. The remaining three are consistency fixes that can land in the same revision.
